Title: Infernal Servitor and Call the Great Beast timing

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
I control only 1 Infernal Servitor, Nergal with a Call the Great Beast on it (with 10 counters).

Nergal puts the 11th counter on the Call the Great Beast. Does the Infernal Servitor 1/ burn because there's a moment where I control no infernal vampire at all 2/ not burn because the Call the Great Beast effect is resolved instantaneously so when Nergal is burned, the Great Beast is there?

Thanks.

Name: Infernal Servitor
Cardtype: Ally
Cost: 1 pool
Discipline: Daimoinon
Unique demon with 2 life. 1 strength, 3 bleed. Requires an infernal vampire.
[dai] Move the servitor to the ready region when recruited. Remove her from the game if she successfully performs an action (after resolution) or if you control no infernal vampires.
[DAI] As above, and the servitor may play cards requiring Daimoinon [dai] or Obfuscate [obf] as a vampire.

Name: Call the Great Beast
[BL:R1, KMW:PB]
Cardtype: Action
Clan: Baali
Cost: 1 blood
+1 stealth action.
Put this card on the acting Baali and put X ritual counters on it, where X is the capacity of this Baali. This Baali may put a ritual counter on this card as a +1 stealth action. When this card has more than 10 ritual counters, burn this Baali and choose three Disciplines. This card becomes a unique clanless independent infernal vampire with 9 capacity, 4 strength and 3 bleed. The Great Beast has the chosen three Disciplines at superior. Move 9 blood to him from the blood bank. The Great Beast can enter combat with any ready minion controlled by another Methuselah as a  action and can prevent 1 damage each combat.

Prince of Paris, France

Ratings Coordinator, Rules Director

Messages.Author: Malachy
Messages.Body:
I would think that processes "happening" in the card text have no time windows between them. Like you can stockpile Spying Mission (only usable on a successful bleed but in the end it is not successful) or one would die due to a political action which happens to give her pool so she stays alive, and so on...

In this case I'm convinced Infernal Servitor doesn't get removed because it can't interfere in CtGB's inner changes so to speak

Of course IANP, and I just guess how these "happenings in card texts" work...

Let's say A has 2 pool and a minion. B bleeds A with Frederick the Weak for one, having Changeling Skin Mask also. A's minion attempts to block, and Frederick plays Lost in Crowds. He increases bleed with Old Friend's making it for two. A cannot block and is forced to remove all of his pool. He is ousted. When exactly does he remove his only minion from play? Or, should he remove his minion first or should he remove his Powerbase: Montreal before that?

Ignorance is bliss.
Cypher, Matrix

Messages.Author: KevinM
Messages.Body:
How does the timing of removal from play of cards owned by an ousted Methuselah matter in any way?

Technically, rulebook 9.1 states "If you are ousted, all the cards you control are removed from the game." So, the answer is: You remove all of your cards at the same time.

Messages.Author: Juggernaut1981
Messages.Body:
I would say that you cannot trigger the Infernal Servitor text in the middle of resolving the Great Beast.

1) Great Beast Action occurs
a) Vampire with Great Beast Burns
b) Great Beast turns into Vampire
2) Great Beast Action resolves
3) Infernal Servitor checks for Infernal Vampires and finds Great Beast.

Retired Baron of Sydney, Australia, 418

Messages.Author: Juggernaut1981
Messages.Body:
Ankha,
I still dispute the "payment of costs happens at the same time as effect" (which is the basis of Eternals of Sirius/Villein on 1 pool argument). That should be a different scenario; there is no payment involved in using CtGB.

The burning of the minion is not a cost of the Call the Great Beast. It is one of the effects of resolving the action to put a counter on CtGB. Since burning the vampire, choosing the disciplines and putting the Beast into play are all effects of putting the counter on CtGB, the Infernal Servitor sees them resolve concurrently (they are the immediate resolution of effects from the action of putting on the counter).
